title: Talk Therapy is Speech - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: A federal court in D.C. struck down the ban on out-of-state therapists doing teletherapy with D.C. clients on First Amendment grounds, six years after counselor Elizabeth Brokamp and the Institute for Justice sued. Alex Tabarrok argues the win should extend to physicians and that the right fix is not interstate compacts or federal licensure but letting patients consult any doctor licensed in any state.

insights.claim: The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia struck down a D.C. law that barred out-of-jurisdiction therapists from conducting online teletherapy with clients in D.C., holding the restriction violated the First Amendment.

themes.theme: Free the patient, not the licensor

insights.claim: The binding constraint in cross-state care is not who issues medical licenses but that patients are forbidden from choosing a doctor licensed in another state — so the fix is patient-side freedom, keeping state-level licensing intact.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: A reform path that needs no new federal agency or compact is politically cheaper and could arrive faster than consensus expects.
insights.quote: The real issue isn’t who licenses doctors. It’s that patients are forbidden from choosing a licensed doctor in another state.
